_description: Cross-driver n-gram corpus for manual corrections. Every Backspace is a token of the typing chain on every driver: it ends a bigram and a trigram ('x[BS]', 'yx[BS]'), and what follows it continues from it ('[BS]x', 'y[BS]x', ...) up to the heptagrams. Each vector is replayed as one typing entry per flush, for the same application, through the Windows (KLW_WalkTypingEntry), macOS (aggregator walk_typing) and Linux (aggregate_walker.walk with a carried context) walkers. 'expected' lists, for each of the seven n-gram families, every token whose typed count c is above zero and that count; a family absent from the batch or with no such token is {}. The comparison is exact, so a token a walker adds or drops fails on that driver.

vectors.description: The character typed after a correction pairs with it
Consecutive corrections chain with each other and with the next character
A pause at the keystroke threshold before the next character breaks the sequence
A correction that ends one flush still chains with the first character of the next
